accuracy.evidence: Matched to Common Core F-IF.1 (each input in the domain has exactly one output in the range) and F-IF.5 (relate the domain to the quantitative relationship it describes), and to the topic's evidence lines (state domain and range from a graph, give a sensible domain for a real model, explain why √x is restricted). Every value checked by hand: √9, √4, √0 = 3, 2, 0 and √(−4) not real; x² − 1 on −2 ≤ x ≤ 3 gives endpoint outputs 3 and 8 and vertex (0, −1), so range −1 ≤ y ≤ 8; h(t) = 20t − 5t² = 5t(4 − t) is 0 at t = 0 and 4, maximum h(2) = 20; 1/(x − 2) excludes x = 2 and never equals 0; C(n) = 12n for n = 0..8 gives 0..96 in steps of 12. Challenge answers rechecked: √(x − 3) needs x ≥ 3; x² on −1 ≤ x ≤ 2 has range 0 ≤ y ≤ 4; 5/(x + 1) excludes −1; 30 − 6t reaches 0 at t = 5; x² + 2 has range y ≥ 2. Mastery m4: x² − 4x = (x − 2)² − 4, minimum −4, g(5) = 5.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the common domain-and-range errors: taking the range from endpoint values and missing a turning point (step 3 prediction 3 ≤ y ≤ 8, m4, challenge tag 'end'), swapping domain and range (picking −1 ≤ x ≤ 8 for the domain, tag 'swap'), writing x ≥ 0 for √(x − 3) instead of solving the inequality (p1, tag 'neg'), the wrong excluded value for a denominator (x ≠ 1 for 5/(x + 1), tag 'zero'), accepting any value the formula takes regardless of context (t = 5 for the ball, tag 'ctx') and treating counted quantities as continuous (joined ticket line, tag 'disc').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdomrng is about which inputs and outputs a function admits: a square-root machine that jams on a negative input, a parabola whose x-shadow and y-shadow are drawn as bands with the vertex marked, a projectile path whose end is dragged until h = 0, a draggable point that reports division by zero at the asymptote, and ticket costs that refuse to be joined. flagoddev (symmetry), flagexpg (exponential graphs), flaggradf (gradient sketching) and flagdomain (subject vocabulary) share none of these mechanics; the shingle gate is under 30% against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner meets each restriction before the rule: the machine shows outputs 3, 2, 0 and then jams on −4; the y-shadow visibly dips to the vertex below both endpoints; dragging past t = 4 shows a negative height in red; sliding towards x = 2 makes the output shoot off and then report 1 ÷ 0; the joined ticket line prompts the half-ticket objection. Step text then states the domain and range.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options: 0 as the input √x cannot take, 3 ≤ y ≤ 8 (endpoints only) for the range, 'Yes, any t works in the formula' for t = 5, and 0 or −2 as the excluded value of 1/(x − 2). Each is settled by what the canvas shows in that step.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge items, each with two tagged wrong answers (neg, zero, end, swap, ctx, disc); every message names the slip, e.g. 'The endpoints are not always the extremes. Check for a turning point in between.' and 'Domain is about inputs (x); range is about outputs (y). Those are swapped.' Wrong answer buttons inside the lab steps also explain the slip ('Those are y-values. The domain is about x.').

readability.evidence: Learner text uses short sentences and the precise terms (domain, range, input, output, turning point, vertex, denominator, discrete) with each defined by example; validate_lessons passes the learner and adult readability limits.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate clean. Each learner paragraph covers one idea (definitions, algebraic restrictions, reading from graphs, context and discreteness) and each lab step tests one of them.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android light and iPhone 13 dark screenshots after Show me on every step; the first pass let the 1/(x − 2) branches run below the plot into the status line, so curves are now clipped to the plot window; messages wrap; drag on the projectile and the hyperbola and taps on the machine inputs were tested on iPhone 13 with no page errors.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin (Feed x = n, Squash onto x-axis / y-axis, t ± 0.5, x ± 0.5, Join the dots, and labelled answer buttons); the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each output, reading and challenge question; walk.cjs reports axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
